guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our clearest matchup advantage is Missouri’s defense against Mississippi State’s ability to create scoring opportunities. Our numbers also favor Missouri’s pass defense against the Mississippi State passing game. That matters, but the market is already pricing much of the same advantage we see, leaving little meaningful disagreement to exploit.

Missouri’s opener provided encouraging passing context, with Austin Simmons completing 17 of 19 attempts for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. We are not treating one performance as proof that the passing game has solved everything, especially because our longer-run numbers remain less favorable when Missouri throws against the Mississippi State pass defense. We also have to account for a Missouri defense that returned only two starters, even after adding experienced SEC transfers Robert Woodyard Jr. and Chris Graves Jr. With the strongest Missouri arguments largely reflected in the market and legitimate uncertainty elsewhere, we do not see enough value to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Mississippi State’s passing offense against Missouri’s rebuilt defense. Our efficiency numbers favor Missouri in that matchup, particularly in preventing productive possessions, but the personnel turnover makes this an important test of how quickly the new group has come together. If Missouri’s pass defense performs near our longer-run expectation, Mississippi State may struggle to generate enough scoring chances to change the game’s shape.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 victory over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while allowing 198 total yards.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime and outgained the Golden Lions 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone opportunities against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri's defense forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons started Missouri's opener and completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in his Missouri debut.
Simmons is Missouri's first-team quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers listed as the backup.
Zollers played in the opener, completing 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards and scoring on a five-yard run.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed starting offensive line is LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Green, Giudice and Peagler are returning offensive-line starters from 2025; Missouri lost starting center Connor Tollison and tackle Keagen Trost.
Luke Work, Missouri's listed starting right tackle, previously played at Mississippi State.
Reserve guard Zack Owens previously played at Mississippi State in addition to Clemson and Colorado.
Jamal Roberts is listed as Missouri's starting running back and rushed 13 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the opener.
Missouri lists Cayden Lee, Donovan Olugbode and Naeshaun Montgomery or Caleb Goodie Sr. as its starting wide receivers.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee caught five passes for 89 yards in his Missouri debut, including a 47-yard touchdown from former Ole Miss teammate Austin Simmons.
Donovan Olugbode recorded the first 100-yard receiving game of his career and caught two touchdown passes in the opener.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned only two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including both starting safeties, two cornerbacks, two linebackers and four defensive-front players.
Returning defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb combined for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also had 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith, listed as Missouri's starting JACK defender, recorded 4.0 sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025.
Missouri added experienced SEC transfers Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker and Chris Graves Jr. at cornerback; both are listed as starters.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and made 67 tackles, while Graves started nine games for Ole Miss in 2025.
Jeremiah Beasley led Missouri with seven tackles in the season-opening win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is in his first season in the role.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri as tight ends coach in January 2026, and Chop Harbin joined as defensive line coach.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season while continuing to coach linebackers.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, ranking eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri recorded a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances in 2025.
Missouri rushed for 31 touchdowns in 2025 and added three rushing touchdowns in the 2026 opener.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, ranking eighth nationally in total defense and 17th in scoring defense.
Missouri allowed 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game in 2025.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri allowed 198 total yards, 3.7 yards per play and a 23% third-down conversion rate.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is Missouri's listed placekicker and made a 32-yard field goal plus all seven extra-point attempts in the opener.
Florida State transfer Brunno Reus is listed as Missouri's first-team punter, kickoff specialist and holder.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as Missouri's primary punt and kickoff returner and had a 23-yard punt return in the opener.

series_context.fact: Missouri defeated Mississippi State 49-27 in Columbia on Nov. 15, 2025.
Ahmad Hardy rushed 25 times for 300 yards and three touchdowns against Mississippi State in 2025.
Darris Smith recorded 3.0 tackles for loss against Mississippi State in 2025.
Missouri returned an interception for a touchdown against Mississippi State in the 2025 meeting.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri is scheduled to play at Mississippi State on Sept. 26, 2026 in its first SEC game of the season.
Missouri entered the Kansas game 1-0 and ranked No. 25 in both the AP and Coaches polls.
